assets.source_text: Good morning, everyone. The school music room is open for a short song workshop this Saturday. Please come to Music Room 2 at eleven o'clock. We will practise two easy songs. Bring a pencil. You do not need to bring an instrument because our school has drums and keyboards. The workshop ends at twelve o'clock. To join, write your name on the music list near the office by Friday.

Hi! Can you help me choose something to do this weekend? The zip on my school bag is broken, and I'd rather repair the bag than buy a new one. I can only go out on Sunday afternoon, after two. My aunt can come with me. I'd like to be indoors because the weather might be rainy. I don't mind making a small donation, but I don't want to pay a fixed entry fee. Could you tell me which event would be useful? And please let me know if they can definitely fix the bag.

assets.source_text: I think the Quiet Study Zone is the more practical first pilot. Students have told me that a calm place after class would help them prepare for assessments, and the annex already has desks. Still, we must be careful about the questionnaire. It was sent just before exam week, when students might have been thinking more about silent study than they usually do. I also see the value of a Project Studio for teamwork. Because we can fund only one room, I'd begin with the quiet annex and ask students how often they actually use it. After four weeks, we could collect feedback from students who wanted a project room, too. Then the council would have better evidence before choosing any permanent plan.
